title: Larry Ellison Risk Exposed by Paramount and Oracle Debt Binges
source_used: Bloomberg (text read on the Yahoo Finance copy)
key_facts: Paramount Skydance took on about $52 billion of new debt this week ($30bn investment-grade bonds, $12.4bn junk bonds, $9.46bn loans) to buy Warner Bros. Discovery; the package wrapped Wednesday 30 Sep
Oracle has nearly doubled long-term debt to more than $160 billion in two years for its AI computing build and is now the fifth-largest US corporate bond borrower (Bloomberg index data)
Both rest on Larry Ellison: a family trust guaranteed a large part of about $47 billion of equity for the Paramount deal and the family pledged to help cut leverage
Ellison's fortune has fallen almost $200 billion from its peak to about $192 billion, mostly through Oracle stock, which is down more than 50 percent in a year
S&P cut Oracle to BBB- in July and Paramount to BB last month
Investors and an S&P analyst say the two credits are linked through one sponsor; Oracle and Paramount did not comment
quote_evidence: "You have to consider your total Larry Ellison risk," Goodman said, adding that investors should regard Oracle and Paramount as related bets rather than completely separate credits.

Oracle, for its part, has nearly doubled its long-term debt to more than $160 billion over the past two years, as the company refashions itself as a provider of computing power for artificial intelligence work.
"Part of the Paramount credit story is tied to confidence in the Oracle story, because Larry Ellison's financial strength sits behind both."
why_it_matters_hint: Two of the biggest corporate borrowers in America now lean on one man whose wealth rides on an AI stock
